title: Plain Naan
subtitle: Griddle-cooked leavened flatbread
excerpt: Soft, pillowy flatbreads made from a yeasted dough with yoghurt, cooked in a very hot pan until blistered and charred in places. Brushed with butter straight from the pan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Naan (or nan) is a leavened flatbread baked in a tandoor oven across South and Central Asia. The home version uses a very hot cast-iron pan or griddle to approximate the high heat of a tandoor, and yoghurt in the dough contributes softness and a slight tang.

recipeTools.notes: For the high, even heat needed to blister the naan.

content.text: Naan cooked at home in a cast-iron pan is very close to the real thing. The pan needs to be very hot, much hotter than most people attempt, so that the naan blisters and chars on the surface while remaining soft inside. The dough uses yoghurt for tenderness and a small amount of yeast for the slight puff. A brush of melted butter at the end is not optional.

Combine the flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in a large bowl. Make a well in the centre and add the yoghurt, warm milk, and oil. Mix to a rough dough, then knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be soft but not sticky.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until roughly doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into a teardrop shape, about 3 to 4 mm thick.

Heat a cast-iron pan over the highest possible heat until very hot and beginning to smoke. Lay a naan in the dry pan and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles form across the surface and the underside has dark char marks. Flip and cook for 1 minute.
Transfer to a plate and brush immediately with melted butter. Keep warm under a clean cloth while cooking the remaining naan. Serve as soon as possible.
